editor.saved_tftp: codeplug.bin was saved, with the DMR ID database when the codeplug has one. With the radio in USB network mode, send it with curl, which announces the file size the radio needs to take the database: curl -T codeplug.bin tftp://<radio address>/codeplug.bin. The radio also takes the database alone as iddb.bin (see the USB network chapter of the documentation).

editor.radio_err.unknown_radio: The radio reports itself as {board}, which the codeplug editor does not know. Reload the page to get the latest version. If the radio is still unknown, report the problem.
editor.radio_err.read_refused: The radio refused to read at {addr}. Turn the radio off and on, then read it again. If it refuses again, report the problem.
editor.radio_err.no_storage: This radio's memory chip is smaller than Open25-DM32 Classic needs to store a codeplug, so the Codeplug Editor cannot read or write it. The radio does not keep its settings when turned off.
editor.radio_err.write_refused: The radio refused to write the codeplug at {addr}. The codeplug on the radio may be incomplete. Write it again; if the radio refuses again, report the problem.
editor.radio_err.write_no_answer: The radio stopped answering while the codeplug was written (at {addr}). Check that the radio is turned on and the cable is connected, then write it again.
editor.radio_err.storage_foreign: The radio has not been prepared for Open25-DM32 Classic yet, so it cannot store a codeplug. Choose Write to Radio again, then Prepare Radio.
editor.radio_err.storage_claim_failed: The radio did not finish preparing its settings area. Turn it off and on again, then choose Write to Radio again.
editor.radio_err.verify_failed: The radio's codeplug does not match what was written (at {addr}). Write it again.
editor.radio_err.verify_incomplete: The radio stopped returning the codeplug while the write was checked (at {addr}). Check that the radio is turned on and the cable is connected, then write it again.
editor.storage.title: Prepare the Radio
editor.storage.text: The {radio} still holds data from its original firmware in the area where Open25-DM32 Classic stores its settings. Until that area is prepared, the radio cannot store a codeplug, and it does not keep its settings when turned off.
editor.storage.text2: Preparing erases that area (40 KB of the memory chip), which holds part of the original firmware's zones and RX group lists. Open25-DM32 Classic does not use them. The backup taken when Open25-DM32 Classic was installed holds a complete copy: to keep the original channels, open that backup in the Codeplug Editor, which converts them. The calibration is not changed. Preparing takes a few seconds.
editor.storage.done: The {radio} is prepared and can now store a codeplug.
editor.radio_err.iddb_too_big: The DMR ID database does not fit in this radio. Choose fewer regions or shorter text.
editor.radio_err.stopped: Stopped. The codeplug on the radio may be incomplete; write it again.
editor.radio_err.other: The radio connection failed: {error}. Check the cable and that the radio is on, then try again.
report.title: Report a Problem
report.text: Describe the problem and download the report. Attach it to an issue in the Open25-DM32 project.
report.text_send: Send the report to the developers, or download it as a zip file to email. It lists the steps this page took, the errors and your browser's details. It never contains firmware files or backups.
report.describe: What were you doing, and what happened?
report.describe_hint: For example: wrote the codeplug to a DM-1701 over the programming cable; it stopped at 40%.
report.attach_codeplug: Include the codeplug I am editing
report.attach_radio: Include the codeplug last read from the radio
report.attach_note: A codeplug contains your callsign, DMR ID and contacts. Include it when the problem is with reading or writing one.
report.downloaded: Report downloaded. You can attach it to an Open25-DM32 issue.
report.sent: Report sent. Its reference is {id}: mention it if you contact the developers.
report.send_failed: The report could not be sent. Download it instead and email it.
report.reported: This error was reported to the developers automatically (reference {id}). They will review it and work on the underlying problem. Anything you add helps: what you were doing, the radio, the cable.
report.reported_hint: For example: reading the codeplug from a DM-32UV over the programming cable, right after switching it on.
report.reported_short: This error was reported to the developers automatically. They will review it and work on the underlying problem.
report.reported_thanks: Thank you, the details were added to the report.
report.privacy_text: When something fails, this page sends the error, the step it happened in, the page's last steps before it (such as the port chosen, what the radio answered and what the page decided about the codec and the key), the USB cable's chip, your browser's name and the radio model and firmware version to the developers' error tracker (Sentry). For a firmware file you pick: its name, size and checksum; for a file the page can't open, also its type and first 8 bytes. Never your codeplug, callsign, DMR ID or file contents. Reports you send from Report a Problem contain what the dialog lists.
report.text_backend: Send this report to the developers. It always contains the steps this page took and what it decided (codec, key, write plan), the error, the radio model, the firmware versions, the USB cable's chip and your browser's name. The files checked below are sent too.
report.email: Email, if you'd like a reply (optional)
report.email_bad: That email address doesn't look complete. Fix it or leave the field empty.
report.optional_note: Both fields are optional: the report is useful without them.
report.attach_stock_read: The original firmware read from the radio: {name}
report.attach_readout: The firmware read from the radio
report.attach_note_files: Uncheck a file to leave it out. A backup holds your channels, contacts and the radio's calibration.
report.kept: Attached files and your email address are deleted within 90 days.
report.sent_backend: Report sent: {id}. Quote it if you write to us.
report.send_failed_backend: The report could not be sent ({error}). Download it instead and email it.
report.refused.report-gone: the report is no longer there
report.refused.too-many: the report already has the most files it can take
report.refused.too-late: the time to add files to this report has passed
report.refused.too-large: the file is larger than a report can take
report.refused.rate: too many reports from here just now; try again later
report.refused.unreadable: the page could not read it
